Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:1.english: Kafzizei - A vessel that holds three log.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:10.english: And smear it [on her] - When they are soaked in water.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:11.hebrew: פשטינא - עשב שאינו גדל בקומה, אלא הולך ופשט על גבי קרקע:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:11.english: Pashtina - An herb that does not grow upright, but rather spreads along the ground.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:12.english: Charnuga - It is a type of herb that grows near thorns.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:13.english: Roman thorn [higta romita] - It is a species of haga [thorn] that is called romit [Roman].

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:14.english: And take it in rags of linen - They should take that ash in worn-out linen garments in the summer.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:4.hebrew: קום מזוביך - חדלי מזוביך, כמו ויעמוד השמן (מלכים ב ד):
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:4.english: Stop [emitting] your discharge - Cease from your discharge, like "and the oil stopped" (II Kings 4).

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:5.english: And frighten her - He should frighten her without her knowledge, suddenly.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:1:9.english: Barrel seals - [The] seal of a barrel.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:1.english: Let one dig seven pits - Seven pits.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:10.hebrew: אי נקטא - לה בידה חד יומא, פסקה מזובה תרי יומא. אית דגרס: נקטה חדא נימא — גרעין אחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:10.english: If she holds - it in her hand for one day, she ceases from her discharge for two days. Some have the reading: "she holds one *nima*" — [meaning] one grain.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:2.english: Shoots of orlah - Vine shoots of a young vineyard.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:3.english: And let him have her hold a cup of wine - He shall hold a cup of wine in her hand, and she shall sit over the pit.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:4.hebrew: ולוקמה מהא - מעל גומא זו יושיבוה על זו, ועל כל עמידה נימא לה: קום מזוביך:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:4.english: And let one raise her up from this [pit] - [From] over this pit they sit her upon that [one], and at every standing up one says to her: "Arise from your discharge."

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:6.english: And let one anoint her - They anoint her with it.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:8.english: Let one open a barrel of wine for her, for her sake - That is to say, she should drink much wine constantly.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:2:9.english: A barley [grain] that is found in the dung of a white mule - A barley [grain] that is found in the dung of a white mule.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:1.hebrew: לירקונא - דאמרן לעיל, קומא וגביא גילא וכורכמא, תרי בשיכרא ומיעקר:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:1.english: For jaundice - [As] we stated above: gum, alum, and saffron — two [of them] in beer, and one becomes sterile.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:10.english: He should wipe him with his sheet - He should wrap him well in his sheet, or in the sheet of another person ill with this illness.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:11.english: Rav Kahana performed for him - This remedy of the sheet.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:2.hebrew: ואי לא - דלית ליה, אי נמי עביד ולא אהני:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:2.english: And if not - That he does not have [them], or else he did [it] and it was not effective.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:3.english: The head of a shibuta - The head of a fish whose name is shibuta.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:4.english: Of salt - [Meaning] that it is salted.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:7.english: And let him rub him - They should rub him with it.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:8.hebrew: בין תנור לגודא - בין תנור לכותל, במקום חם, שיזיע ויצא החולי:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:8.english: Between [the] oven and the wall - Between [the] oven and the wall, in a warm place, so that he will sweat and the illness will leave.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:3:9.english: One who wishes to warm him - this [patient].

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:1.english: Dripping wax [kira d'nishtrufei] - Wax that floats and drips from a beehive that has become full and overflows.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:10.english: A head of a barḥa - Of a ram.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:11.english: That is placed in pickle - Pickled in vinegar or in brine.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:12.hebrew: דבר אחר חוטרנא - חזיר טלוא בחברבורות, מנומר:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:12.english: "Something else," chutrana - A pig spotted with spots, speckled.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:13.english: From the middle of the garden beds - From the middle of the garden bed, for they are sharp.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:4.english: A donkey foal - [meaning] a young donkey, the offspring of she-donkeys.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:5.english: And let him shave - the sick person.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:6.english: The middle of its head - The middle of its head.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:7.english: And let him let blood for it from its forehead - He should let blood from the foal's forehead.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:8.english: And place it on his head - He should pour the blood onto the shaved area.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:4:9.english: And he should be careful regarding his eyes - That none of this blood enters his eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:5:1.english: Lend me your cloak - Lend me the cloak.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:5:2.english: And I will sleep in it - And I will sleep in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:5:4.english: He wrapped himself [and] slept - He wrapped himself in it and slept in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:5:5.hebrew: נפל פורתא פורתא - קדחה הטלית מחום שריפת החולי שיצא עם הזיעה, ונפלה חתיכות דקות:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:5:5.english: It fell bit by bit - The cloak was scorched from the heat of the burning of the illness that came out with the sweat, and it fell [into] fine pieces.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:6:1.english: And is it permitted - to drink a cup of [sterilizing] roots?

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:6:2.english: You shall not do [this] - Read into it: "You shall not be made [castrated]."

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:6:3.hebrew: ומסתרס מאליו - ואע"ג דסירוס אסור בידים:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:6:3.english: And it becomes castrated on its own - [This is permitted] even though castration directly by hand is prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:6:4.hebrew: והא אמר רב אשי - דההוא לאו סירוס הוא, אלא רמות רוחא נקיטא ליה לתרנגול, ומשניטל הודו הוא מתאבל ואינו משמש; אבל בסירוס, אפילו ממילא אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:6:4.english: Didn't Rav Ashi say - That [case] is not [actual] castration; rather, haughtiness possesses the rooster, and once its glory [i.e., its comb] is removed, it mourns and does not mate; but in [a case of actual] castration, even [if it happens] on its own, it is prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 110b:6:5.hebrew: אלא בסריס - הך דשרי למישתי כוס של עיקרין, במי שהוא סריס כבר עסקינן:
Rashi on Shabbat 110b:6:5.english: Rather, with one who is castrated - [Regarding] this [statement] that it is permitted to drink a cup of [sterilizing] roots, we are dealing with one who is already castrated.

Tosafot on Shabbat 110b:6:1.hebrew: והתניא מניין לסירוס שהוא אסור - וא"ת: אפילו לא אסור סירוס, תיקשי ליה דליתסר משום פריה ורביה! וכ"ת משום דהוי מצי לשנויי ביש לו בנים — הא משמע בסוף הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף סה:) גבי דביתהו דר' חייא, דאי הוה מיפקדה אפריה ורביה לא הוה שתיא סמא דעקרתא אע"ג דהוי לה שתי נקבות ושני זכרים, משום "בבקר זרע [את] זרעך ולערב אל תנח ידך" (קהלת יא); ובאשה — לא שייך סירוס — אוקי במסקנא לרבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, דמחייב בפריה ורביה, בעקרה וזקנה, ולא מוקי ביש לה בנים! ויש לומר: דמסירוס ניחא ליה למפרך, משום דאיכא למ"ד בפרק הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף סא:): כיון דקיימא פריה ורביה — תו לא צריך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 110b:6:1.english: "Wasn't it taught [in a baraita]: From where [is it derived] that castration is prohibited?" - And if you say: Even if castration were not prohibited, it should be difficult for [the Gemara] that it should be prohibited because of [the mitzvah of] procreation! And if you say [that the Gemara did not ask from procreation] because it could have answered [that the remedy is] for one who already has children — behold, it is implied at the end of [the chapter] HaBa Al Yevamto (Yevamot 65b) regarding the wife of Rabbi Ḥiyya, that if she were commanded in procreation, she would not have drunk the sterilizing potion even though she [already] had two daughters and two sons, because of "In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not withhold your hand" (Ecclesiastes 11:6); and regarding a woman — [where] castration does not apply — [the Gemara there] establishes [her case] in the conclusion, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka who obligates [women] in procreation, as [referring to] a barren or elderly woman, and does not establish it as [referring to] one who has children! And one can say: That it was preferable for [the Gemara] to raise the objection from castration, because there is one who says in the chapter HaBa Al Yevamto (Yevamot 61b): Once one has fulfilled procreation, he is no longer required [to continue].

Tosafot on Shabbat 110b:6:2.hebrew: תלמוד לומר ובארצכם לא תעשו - מכם קא דריש. והא דאמר בחגיגה (דף יד:): שאלו את בן זומא: מהו לסרוסי כלבא? אמר להו: בארצכם לא תעשו — כל שבארצכם לא תעשו; התם נפקא לן מארץ, כדמפרש בשאלתות דרב אחאי, דהא חובת הגוף הוא, מה לי בארץ מה לי בחו"ל? אלא האי בארץ — לכל אשר בארץ אתא, והכא מכם דריש, כדפי'. ומה שמפרש בשאלתות דהא דאסר לשתות סמא דעקרתא היינו כרבי יהודה, דאמר דבר שאין מתכוין אסור, ואע"ג דקי"ל כר"ש דשרי — היינו דוקא בשבת, משום דבעינן מלאכת מחשבת, אבל בכל התורה כולה סבירא לן כרבי יהודה — ואין נראה לר"י, דבכל התורה כולה קי"ל כר"ש דשרי, כדמשמע לעיל בפ' המוציא (שבת פא:), דאמרי' דרבי יוחנן סבר כסתם משנה דנזיר חופף ומפספס וכו', והיינו כרבי שמעון דשרי דבר שאינו מתכוין. וכן משמע בפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לד.), דשמואל סבר כר"ש בכל התורה כולה דדבר שאין מתכוין שרי, גבי המקיז דם בבכור, דפסק שמואל התם כר"ש דשרי להקיז, ופריך: עד השתא לא אשמועינן שמואל דדבר שאין מתכוין מותר, דאמר רב חייא בר אשי כו'? ואי יש חילוק בין שבת לדעלמא, איצטריך התם שפיר לפסוק כר"ש, אע"ג דכבר אשמעינן דבשבת הלכה כר"ש! והכא אתיא אפילו לר' שמעון, דפסיק רישיה הוא, דודאי יסתרס בשתיי' כוס עיקרין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 110b:6:2.english: "The verse states: 'And in your land you shall not do'" - It expounds [this from the word] "yourselves" [mikem]. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says in Chagigah (14b): "They asked Ben Zoma: What is [the law regarding] castrating a dog? He said to them: 'In your land you shall not do [this]' — anything that is in your land you shall not do" — there it is derived from "in the land," as is explained in the She'iltot of Rav Achai, for since it is a personal obligation [chovat haguf], what difference is there to me [whether it is] in the Land [of Israel] or outside the Land? Rather, this "in the land" comes [to include] everything that is in the land; whereas here it expounds "yourselves" [mikem], as I explained. And as for what [Rav Achai] explains in the She'iltot, that [the reason] it is prohibited to drink a sterilizing potion [sama d'akarta] is in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah, who says that an unintended act [davar she'ein mitkavein] is prohibited — and even though we hold like Rabbi Shimon that it is permitted, that is specifically on Shabbat because we require purposeful labor [melekhet machshevet], whereas in the entire rest of the Torah we hold like Rabbi Yehudah — this does not appear [correct] to the R"I, for in the entire Torah we hold like Rabbi Shimon that it is permitted, as is implied earlier in the chapter Hamotzi (Shabbat 81b), where we say that Rabbi Yochanan holds like the anonymous Mishnah of "A nazirite may rub and scratch, etc.," and that is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon who permits an unintended act. And so too it is implied in the chapter Kol Pesulei Hamukdashin (Bekhorot 34a), that Shmuel holds like Rabbi Shimon in the entire Torah that an unintended act is permitted, regarding one who lets blood from a firstborn animal, where Shmuel rules there like Rabbi Shimon that it is permitted to let blood, and [the Gemara] asks: "Until now, hasn't Shmuel taught us that an unintended act is permitted, as Rav Chiya bar Ashi said, etc.?" Now, if there were a distinction between Shabbat and elsewhere [in the Torah], it would be quite necessary there to rule like Rabbi Shimon, even though [Shmuel] had already taught us that on Shabbat the halakhah is like Rabbi Shimon! Rather, here [our Gemara] follows even Rabbi Shimon, because it is an inevitable consequence [pesik reishei], for one will certainly become castrated by drinking the cup of roots [kos ikarin].
